subject: Environment
description: UNEP, CITES, WWF, Greenpeace, Indian NGOs / agencies

questions.stem: The UN Environment Programme (UNEP) has its headquarters in:

options.option_text: New York
Nairobi
Geneva
Paris

questions.explanation: UNEP — established after the 1972 Stockholm Conference — is HQed in Nairobi, Kenya, making it the first UN agency based in a developing country. Leads climate, biodiversity and pollution agendas; convenes the UN Environment Assembly (UNEA) every two years. Inger Andersen (Denmark) has been Executive Director since 2019.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species) was signed in 1973 and entered into force in:
questions.explanation: CITES — signed 3 March 1973 in Washington DC (hence sometimes called the Washington Convention), came into force 1 July 1975. Classifies species into three Appendices — I (prohibition of commercial trade, e.g., tiger, elephant, rhino), II (regulated trade), III (regulated unilaterally by one country). India is a member since 1976. 3 March is observed as World Wildlife Day.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The well-known panda logo belongs to the organisation:

options.option_text: Greenpeace
WWF (World Wide Fund for Nature)
IUCN
CITES

questions.explanation: WWF was founded in 1961 (Switzerland) and adopted the giant panda Chi-Chi (at London Zoo) as its logo. Works on biodiversity, climate, freshwater, oceans, food. Named originally World Wildlife Fund; renamed World Wide Fund for Nature in most countries in 1986 (US + Canada kept the older name). Greenpeace was founded in 1971 (Vancouver) around anti-nuclear-testing protests.

questions.stem: The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) is a statutory body under which Indian ministry?

options.option_text: Ministry of Home Affairs
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Power

questions.explanation: CPCB — constituted 1974 under the Water Act — operates under MoEFCC. Sets national standards for air, water and noise; coordinates with the State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs); publishes the National Air Quality Index. Headquartered in Delhi.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: 'World Environment Day' is observed every year on:

options.option_text: 22 April
5 June
21 March
22 May

questions.explanation: World Environment Day — observed on 5 June since 1974 (commemorating the 1972 Stockholm Conference). 2018 host — India; theme 'Beat Plastic Pollution'. Other climate-environment days: 22 April (Earth Day), 21 March (International Day of Forests), 22 May (Biodiversity Day), 8 June (World Oceans Day), 17 June (World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought), 16 September (World Ozone Day).
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The 'Global Environment Facility' (GEF), which funds environmental projects in developing countries, was established in:
questions.explanation: GEF — established 1991 in advance of the Rio Earth Summit (1992) — pools funds from donor countries to support projects on climate, biodiversity, land degradation, international waters, persistent pollutants. Hosted by the World Bank but operationally independent. Complements the Adaptation Fund (under UNFCCC) and the Green Climate Fund (2010).
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: 'Silent Spring', the 1962 book that spurred the modern environmental movement, was written by:

options.option_text: Wangari Maathai
Rachel Carson
Aldo Leopold
Greta Thunberg

questions.explanation: Rachel Carson (American marine biologist / conservationist) wrote 'Silent Spring' (1962), exposing the dangers of DDT and other pesticides — especially their biomagnification up the food chain into fish-eating birds. Triggered the US ban on DDT (1972) and the founding of the EPA. Wangari Maathai — Kenyan, founded the Green Belt Movement, Nobel Peace 2004. Aldo Leopold — 'A Sand County Almanac'. Greta Thunberg — Swedish youth climate activist.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The Ramsar Convention (1971) primarily focuses on the conservation and sustainable use of which type of ecosystem?

options.option_text: Coral reef ecosystems and marine biodiversity zones
Wetlands of international importance for waterfowl
Tropical rainforests and their associated biodiversity
High-altitude mountain and alpine tundra ecosystems

questions.explanation: The Ramsar Convention signed in Ramsar, Iran in 1971 is the intergovernmental treaty dedicated to the conservation and wise use of wetlands, recognising their role as habitats for waterfowl. Coral reefs are addressed under the International Coral Reef Initiative, not Ramsar.

questions.stem: The Montreal Protocol (1987) was specifically designed to phase out substances that cause depletion of which component of the atmosphere?

options.option_text: The tropospheric ozone that filters urban pollutants
The stratospheric ozone layer shielding UV radiation
Carbon dioxide concentrations driving climate warming
Methane and nitrous oxide causing greenhouse effects

questions.explanation: The Montreal Protocol targets ozone-depleting substances (ODS) such as CFCs and HCFCs that destroy stratospheric ozone, which shields Earth from harmful ultraviolet radiation. Carbon dioxide and methane are covered under the UNFCCC/Kyoto Protocol, not Montreal.

questions.stem: Which of the following international conventions specifically regulates the transboundary movement and disposal of hazardous wastes between countries?

options.option_text: Stockholm Convention on persistent organic pollutants
Basel Convention on transboundary hazardous waste movement
Rotterdam Convention on prior informed consent procedure
Minamata Convention on mercury and its compounds globally

questions.explanation: The Basel Convention (1989) controls transboundary movement of hazardous wastes and their disposal, aiming to protect developing nations from becoming dumping grounds. Stockholm targets POPs, Rotterdam governs chemical trade via Prior Informed Consent, and Minamata specifically addresses mercury — all are distinct from Basel.

questions.stem: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) was jointly established in 1988 by which two bodies?

options.option_text: UNEP and the World Meteorological Organization (WMO)
UNDP and the UN Framework Convention secretariat body
UNEP and the United Nations Development Programme only
WMO and the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)

questions.explanation: IPCC was established in 1988 jointly by UNEP (which deals with environment) and WMO (which deals with meteorology/climate science). It does not conduct original research but assesses existing scientific literature. UNDP and FAO are commonly confused distractors — neither co-founded IPCC.

questions.stem: Under the Kyoto Protocol, which mechanism allows Annex-I (developed) countries to earn certified emission reduction credits by financing clean-energy projects in developing countries?

options.option_text: Joint Implementation (JI) between two Annex-I nations
Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) in non-Annex-I nations
International Emissions Trading Scheme (ETS) framework
Technology Transfer Protocol (TTP) under the UNFCCC body

questions.explanation: CDM (Article 12 of Kyoto Protocol) lets developed (Annex-I) countries invest in emission-reduction projects in developing (non-Annex-I) countries and earn Certified Emission Reductions (CERs). Joint Implementation is similar but operates between two Annex-I countries — a very common exam confusion with CDM.

questions.stem: The Minamata Convention (2017) on mercury is named after a Japanese city where thousands suffered neurological damage. What was the source of contamination in the original Minamata disease case?

options.option_text: Lead compounds discharged from automobile battery factories
Mercury-containing wastewater from a chemical plastics plant
Arsenic leachate released from large gold mining operations
Cadmium effluents from zinc and lead smelting industries

questions.explanation: Minamata disease (1950s–60s) was caused by methylmercury discharged into Minamata Bay by the Chisso Corporation's chemical plant (producing acetaldehyde). Bioaccumulation in fish poisoned coastal communities. Cadmium poisoning causing Itai-itai disease in Japan is a separate incident — a frequent examiner trap alongside Minamata.

questions.stem: The Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES) — often called the 'biodiversity IPCC' — was established in which year, and where is its permanent secretariat located?

options.option_text: Established in 2010, secretariat hosted in Geneva, Switzerland
Established in 2012, secretariat hosted in Bonn, Germany
Established in 2005, secretariat hosted in Nairobi, Kenya
Established in 2015, secretariat hosted in New York, USA

questions.explanation: IPBES was established in April 2012 in Panama City following a UNEP decision and its secretariat is hosted by Germany in Bonn (same city as the UNFCCC secretariat). Nairobi is the UNEP headquarters and a common confusion. 2010 is the year the Nagoya Protocol was adopted, not IPBES's founding — a deliberate distractor.
